thread:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for release model-serving:v3.1.0 -> applying to 8% of prod-us replicas. Canary deployment: model-svc-canary-*.

leah: paging 12: complaining about a spike in 502/503s hitting the inference gateway. Noticing many canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff. @omar are you seeing anything on infra side?

omar: I'm on it. grabbing logs: `kubectl -n prod-us logs model-svc-canary-2c9b -c init` - init container is stuck on "fetching kv-store" with repeated timeouts. Main container retries then OOMs.

nina: HPA for canary has minReplicas:0, scaleTargetCPU: 90%, but the readiness probe is failing so pods are created then immediately killed and HPA keeps adjusting -> scale thrash. This is causing more 5xx as traffic sometimes lands on partially initialized pods.

felix: support lists ~7 customers seeing higher latencies and intermittent 502s to /v1/generate since 11:21. Marking as potential customer-impacting. Sending heads up to CS.

omar: root cause hypothesis: v3.1.0 added an init sidecar that downloads a large shard from S3 and we don't have a timeout/backoff. It stalls under certain node-local network conditions. When init hangs, kubelet kills pod after probe timeout then HPA spins new ones.

mia: we have a LaunchDarkly flag `canary.routing.model-svc-v3` controlling traffic to the canary. I can toggle it to stop routing to canary instantly. Recommend flipping first, then scale canary to zero and rollback image.

incident-bot: @leah acknowledged incident. Severity set to sev2. Runbook: k8s-deploy-failure. Channel: #inc-1845501200 created.

leah: mia please flip the flag, Omar prepare scale/rollback commands and a patch to set HPA minReplicas=1. I'll coordinate customer comms.

mia: flipping flag now -> `ldctl set canary.routing.model-svc-v3 false` :white_check_mark: New traffic should stop hitting canary within ~20s.

omar: verifying traffic: LB metrics show canary request rate dropping. scaling down canary: `kubectl -n prod-us scale deployment model-svc-canary --replicas=0` -> pods terminating.

omar: rolling back canary image to v3.0.7 as a safety measure: `kubectl -n prod-us set image deployment/model-svc-canary model=redwood/model-serving:v3.0.7` followed by `kubectl rollout status deployment/model-svc-canary`. Applied.

nina: HPA patch: `kubectl -n prod-us patch hpa model-svc-canary -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1}}'` and lowering target CPU to 500m so it doesn't overshoot. Applying to main deployment too.

omar: logs from failed inits show S3 GET timeout then repeated retries without exponential backoff. I'll add a safety timeout to the init container and a node-local caching check in the manifest PR. PR: https://github.com/redwood/model-serving/pull/427

felix: customer comm draft posted in #support-drafts. Notifying the seven affected accounts with an explanation: we paused canary rollout and rolled back to the previous image, no action required by customers, postmortem to follow in 4 hours.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated to monitoring. Automated alert suppression enabled for the canary group for 45m to avoid noisy pages while we validate.

leah: handoff: I'm stepping out at 1845501365, handing active watch to @omar. Next steps captured below:
- collect full pod init logs and kubelet events for the crashed canaries
- run a memory + network perf test for the init sidecar under simulated node conditions
- merge manifest PR with init timeout and readiness probe improvements after validation
- re-run canary rollout in low-traffic window with observability hooks enabled
- write postmortem with timeline, RCA, and customer-facing summary

omar: ack. I'll coordinate with nina to validate metrics and with mia to confirm flag state during re-roll. I'll update this thread with any changes.

incident-bot: Channel will be archived in 3h. Closing active paging loop.

felix: final support note: customers informed, CS context added to affected accounts, offering 1:1 follow ups if needed. Thanks everyone.

leah: good work team. quick kill-switch flip avoided further customer impact. We'll capture the manifest mistake in the postmortem and add a test to catch init-sidecar timeouts in the CI pre-rollout checks. :thumbsup:
